We’re seeking curious minds like yours to collaborate with full-time engineers and cross functional teammates, learn development standard methodologies, and gain practical software engineering experience.
Software engineering interns are fully integrated into software engineering teams across our Product and Technology organization. Interns spend their summer pushing production-level code to make lasting contributions across MongoDB’s products and services for our internal teams, external customers, and developer end users.
This is a 12-week internship starting in May or June 2027.
What we are looking for in you (qualifications)
In the process of receiving a Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
Have a foundation in computer science theory, with proficiencies in data structures, algorithms, and software design.
Fluent in any one of the following programming languages: Java, Python, Go, C++, Javascript, Node.js - or a comparable object-oriented programming language.
Have a minimum of one quarter/semester remaining in university studies after the internship concludes. Graduation date in Fall 2027, Spring 2028, Summer 2028, Fall 2028, Spring 2029 or Summer 2029.
Must be authorized to work in the United States.

Authentic Culture: A workplace where you are encouraged to bring your whole self to work, we believe that Embracing the Power of Differences is the best way to broaden our own perspectives and foster innovation.
Personalized Mentorship: Pair up with an engineering Mentor, a Program Advisor from the Early Talent Recruitment Team, and an Employee Resource Group (ERG) Guide to foster your growth.
Career Coaching Sessions: Access to a tailored training program designed uniquely for interns’ personal and professional development.

Path to Full-Time: A chance to see if MongoDB is where you see yourself long term with the possibility of receiving a full time offer at the end of the summer!

Transform your career by becoming the Chief of Staff (CoS) to MongoDB’s Chief Information Officer, working directly with executives and the leadership team across MongoDB, including but not limited to within the IT organization.
The Role
As a senior leader in technology strategy and operations, the Chief of Staff acts as a key force multiplier for the CIO.
This role requires deep technical knowledge in enterprise systems, technology portfolio management, IT governance, systems analysis, and technology operations to support executive decision-making, enterprise technology investments, and organizational execution across the IT function.
You will run the operating rhythm of the Office of the CIO, lead the IT Program Management Office (ITPMO) that governs the IT portfolio and drive strategic program execution.
You possess the ability to blend strategic direction with hands-on tactical execution: shaping the CIO’s agenda, translating IT strategy into plans and measurable outcomes, and making sure decisions are made on time and followed through.
The role requires evaluating enterprise technology portfolios, identifying technical dependencies and implementation risks, assessing enterprise systems and technology investments, and translating complex technology requirements into governance, prioritization, and execution plans.
You will operate as a versatile, right-hand to help manage initiatives, demonstrating excellent program management and organizational skills, building the mechanisms that help IT scale.
The role also requires applying technical and analytical expertise to enterprise technology initiatives, evaluating systems-level dependencies and risks, and translating complex IT requirements into portfolio decisions and execution plans.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Palo Alto, CA for our hybrid working model.
What You’ll Do
CIO leverage and prioritization: Shape and manage the CIO’s agenda, ensuring time and focus go to the highest-value priorities. Act as a trusted advisor and thought partner, framing decisions with clear options and trade-offs.
Operating rhythm: Design and run the IT operating cadence, including IT leadership team meetings, QBRs, planning cycles, offsites, and executive and board readouts. Build workback plans, track commitments, and surface risks early.
Strategy and planning: Partner with CIO Leadership team to translate IT strategy into annual and quarterly objectives, OKRs, and plans, and track progress against them.
Strategy and planning: Partner with IT leaders to evaluate strategic technology initiatives involving enterprise applications, data platforms, AI capabilities, cloud technologies, cybersecurity programs, and enterprise architecture priorities.
Influence: Collaborate, influence and align with CIO Leadership, peers, and other key stakeholders as needed towards the objectives that we are driving in terms of IT strategy. You are comfortable and possess the ability to push back, question assumptions and influence direction without authority.
ITPMO and portfolio governance: Lead the ITPMO and maintain a single view of the IT portfolio: status, risks, dependencies, value, and alignment to company priorities. You will lead and govern a portfolio consisting of enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, cloud services, infrastructure modernization initiatives, data and analytics platforms, cybersecurity programs, enterprise integrations, AI-enabled capabilities, and digital transformation initiatives. Establish governance processes to evaluate implementation complexity, technical dependencies, resource requirements, architecture impacts, operational readiness, and business value.
Portfolio analysis and governance: Assess cross-functional IT initiatives, including dependencies, implementation risks, resource constraints, and alignment to enterprise technology priorities, to support portfolio prioritization and investment decisions. Analyze enterprise technology initiatives involving business applications, cloud platforms, enterprise integrations, identity and access management systems, cybersecurity controls, analytics environments, and AI adoption programs. Apply knowledge of enterprise systems, systems analysis, IT governance, and technology lifecycle management to assess implementation risks, technical interdependencies, architecture considerations, and operational impacts.
Technology strategy and enterprise systems analysis: Evaluate enterprise technology roadmaps, systems integration requirements, enterprise architecture dependencies, data and AI initiatives, and digital transformation programs. Apply expertise in enterprise systems, technology governance frameworks, systems analysis methodologies, and IT operations to support technology investment decisions and long-term planning.
Strategic program execution: Oversee CIO-sponsored, cross-pillar programs and special projects. Oversee enterprise technology transformation initiatives, including cloud migrations, enterprise application deployments, process automation efforts, enterprise data initiatives, AI adoption programs, and systems integration projects. Partner with DRIs to define, resource, and deliver them, and to remove blockers and hold owners accountable.
Financial and resource partnership: Partner with Finance and IT leaders on budget, forecasting, headcount, and vendor and SaaS spend. Evaluate technology investment proposals, cloud consumption forecasts, infrastructure expenditures, software licensing strategies, SaaS contracts, and vendor capabilities to support prioritization and investment decisions. Assess expected business value, implementation complexity, ongoing operating costs, technical risks, and resource requirements associated with major technology investments.
People priorities and HR partnership: Partner with the HR Business Leader on organizational priorities, leadership transitions, and organizational change initiatives. Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with sound judgement.
Executive communications: Draft and quality-check CIO and leadership communications, including board materials, all-hands content, and IT-wide updates. Develop executive-level communications and board materials that synthesize complex technology topics including enterprise application strategy, technology portfolio performance, cybersecurity initiatives, cloud transformation, AI adoption, and digital modernization efforts into actionable recommendations.
Cross-functional alignment: Partner with Chiefs of Staff and leaders across the executive team. Represent the CIO where appropriate and manage through influence.
Team leadership: Develop and lead the PMO team, strengthening project management capabilities, operational excellence, and portfolio management. Establish consistent standards, drive accountability, and foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and effective execution across IT.
Continuous improvement: Define delivery standards and ways of working, and use data and AI-enabled tools to make governance, reporting, and executive support faster and more scalable. Leverage enterprise systems expertise, workflow automation technologies, analytics platforms, AI-enabled solutions, and technology management best practices to continuously improve governance, reporting, portfolio management, and operational effectiveness.
What You’ll Bring
10+ years of experience in enterprise IT strategy, technology portfolio management, IT program management, or technology operations, ideally within a high-growth technology company.
Experience managing and governing complex enterprise technology portfolios involving enterprise applications, cloud platforms, infrastructure services, cybersecurity programs, systems integrations, data and analytics environments, AI-enabled technologies, and digital transformation initiatives. Demonstrated ability to evaluate enterprise systems, architecture dependencies, implementation risks, technical tradeoffs, and operational impacts across interconnected technology environments.
Experience evaluating program dependencies, implementation risks, and resource constraints to inform prioritization and execution.
Proven ability to design and run governance frameworks, operating cadences, and decision processes, and to manage complex, cross-functional programs end to end.
Financial acumen: comfort with budgets, forecasting, and investment prioritization.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, including board-ready materials that turn complex information into clear recommendations.
Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills; you use data to guide trade-offs and design for scale.
High EQ, low ego, and sound judgment. You build trust quickly and handle confidential information with discretion.
AI-fluent: you apply AI and automation in your own work and in how your teams operate.
Demonstrated experience governing technology portfolios that include areas such as enterprise applications, infrastructure, security, SaaS, or related IT services and delivery. Familiarity with IT delivery and technology portfolios, agile practices, and change management is beneficial.
Bachelor's degree or higher in Information Systems, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or a closely related technical field that provides specialized preparation in enterprise systems, systems analysis, technology architecture, cloud technologies, software and platform lifecycles, enterprise integrations, information management, cybersecurity, data systems, and IT governance.
Flexible schedule; occasional domestic or international travel. Bachelor’s degree required; MBA a plus.
What Success Looks Like
The CIO’s time and focus are aligned to the highest-value priorities, and decisions happen on schedule.
IT’s strategic initiatives are governed through one transparent portfolio, with clear status, risks, and ownership.
IT investments align to company objectives and OKRs, with improved cost transparency and delivery predictability.
The ITPMO is recognized across the company for execution excellence.
What This Is Not
This is not a traditional Chief of Staff or project management role. It is a senior technology strategy and operations leadership position that requires deep technical expertise, the ability to assess enterprise IT roadmaps, requirements, investments, and complex technology initiatives, and the leadership to drive execution across the organization. The role translates the CIO’s strategic vision into actionable priorities, establishes the technical governance frameworks and operating processes needed to scale MongoDB’s IT organization, and leads and develops the Technical Program Management Office (TPMO), driving program governance, portfolio execution, and cross-functional alignment across strategic IT initiatives.

Own the worldwide endpoint architecture and roadmap for macOS, Windows, Linux, and mobile, including management platform strategy, configuration-as-code, application packaging and self-service, and zero-touch provisioning
Lead the release calendar and deployment ring strategy for every endpoint operating system, delivering major and minor updates on time to a published compliance target, with tested rollback and a clear exception path
Administer and evolve MongoDB's endpoint management stack across MDM and UEM platforms, including declarative device management (DDM) on macOS and Windows Autopilot and Autopatch on Windows 11
Own mobile strategy end to end for corporate-owned and BYOD devices across iOS and Android, balancing data protection against an enrollment experience employees will accept MDM where enrollment is appropriate, MAM and app protection policies where it is not
Build and operate MongoDB's Endpoint Digital Employee Experience program: instrument the fleet, define the DEX metrics and SLOs we hold ourselves to, and drive proactive remediation that resolves issues before employees notice them
Partner with InfoSec to implement and continuously improve endpoint security controls, including hardening baselines, patch and vulnerability remediation SLAs, disk encryption and key escrow coverage, device trust, and Conditional Access
Serve as a senior technical escalation point (L3) for complex endpoint issues across the organization
Build automation to reduce manual endpoint operations work and improve reliability and observability, holding the team to configuration-as-code, peer review, and staged rollout
Act as a technical advisor for MongoDB's relationships with endpoint management, DEX, and hardware vendors, and own the endpoint tooling and licensing budget
Hire, coach, and retain a globally distributed team of EUC engineers, and contribute to a culture of technical excellence and self-service

Ensure MongoDB's global endpoint fleet remains reliable, secure, compliant, and scalable across every platform and region as the company grows
Deliver operating system rollouts on time, every cycle, across macOS, Windows, and Linux endpoints

Build and maintain a high-performing international team, and develop engineers into recognized experts in this space
Communicate endpoint strategy, risk, and incidents clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Uphold strong engineering practices across endpoint documentation, automation, and change management
Balance long-term platform architecture work with day-to-day operational support
Define, publish, and manage the team against the metrics for the service

Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent practical experience
8+ years of experience in end user computing, client platform engineering, or endpoint and modern workplace engineering, including 3+ years hiring and leading engineers
Proven experience owning a fleet of several thousand endpoints across multiple countries and time zones
Hands-on depth across all three desktop platforms, not oversight of them: macOS managed through a modern MDM (Jamf Pro, Iru/formerly Kandji, Microsoft Intune, or Omnissa Workspace ONE) with Apple Business (formerly Apple Business Manager) and Automated Device Enrollment; Windows 11 managed through Intune, Windows Autopilot, and Windows Autopatch; Linux endpoints managed as code with Ansible, Fleet, or equivalent
A current understanding of Apple's declarative device management (DDM) model and what its adoption means for software update enforcement, Platform SSO, and configuration and app delivery
Experience with both mobile management models: MDM for corporate-owned devices and MAM/app protection for BYOD, including Intune App Protection Policies, Android Enterprise work profile, and Apple User Enrollment with Managed Apple Accounts
A demonstrated record of delivering major OS rollouts on schedule, with a defined ring strategy, compatibility gating, communications plan, exception process, and rollback path
Experience instrumenting endpoints with a DEX or telemetry platform such as Nexthink, Lakeside SysTrack, ControlUp, 1E, Aternity, Intune Advanced Analytics, or osquery/Fleet, defining a score or SLO from it, and using it to resolve issues proactively
Scripting skills for endpoint automation using infrastructure as code, with fluency in at least one of Bash, Python, Swift, or PowerShell and comfort with Git-based workflows
Experience partnering with InfoSec, Identity, IT Service Delivery, and Workplace teams on cross-functional endpoint initiatives
Experience leading engineers across multiple regions, with a clear approach to coverage, escalation, documentation, and asynchronous decision-making
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical topics to a wide range of audiences
Experience with endpoint documentation and reporting such as fleet compliance dashboards, configuration baselines, and operational runbooks
There will be requirements from time to time to work across multiple time zones as required by the business, including travel
Preferred Qualifications
Jamf Certified Expert, Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate, or equivalent endpoint management certification
Visible standing in the endpoint community — MacAdmins Slack, Jamf Nation, Midwest Management Summit, Penn State MacAdmins — or open-source contributions to projects such as Munki, Installomator, Nudge, swiftDialog, or osquery
Experience supporting a heavily technical employee population, including software engineers with elevated-privilege, virtualization, and local developer and AI tooling needs
Experience with cloud identity and device trust platforms such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID, and with Conditional Access policy design
Familiarity with ITSM practice, service ownership, and Experience Level Agreements (XLAs) alongside traditional SLAs
Experience owning endpoint tooling budget, vendor relationships, and licensing at scale
Experience mentoring other endpoint or systems engineers

In 3 months, you will: Be fully onboarded with a thorough understanding of MongoDB's endpoint estate and policies, have met your team and key partners in every region, and have delivered a written assessment of the worldwide fleet — platform coverage, compliance posture, tooling, gaps, and top risks — with a prioritized plan and any approved roles actively in flight

MongoDB's Global Security Organization (GSO) is looking for a Principal Security Engineer. The GSO secures MongoDB's products, infrastructure, and the trust our customers place in us — spanning product security, corporate security, and risk, and working across engineering, go-to-market, and corporate development to keep security moving at the same speed as the business.
The Principal Security Engineer will serve as a senior technical anchor for the team. This is a deep individual-contributor role that will stay hands-on with hard security and architecture problems, form sharp independent opinions, and know how to debate, align, and commit once GSO has made a call.
Key topic areas will include collaborating with our product teams to ensure identity and permission models meet customer needs for our new autonomous agent platform and working with integration security teams to push the envelope on automated detection, reproduction, and remediation of security vulnerabilities via AI. What we need here is depth, judgment, and the ability to build up the bench of senior technical talent around you.
This role can be based out of our NYC or Seattle office or remotely in the North America region.
Responsibilities
Maintain real technical depth in security and in MongoDB's product architecture — compute, network, and storage — deep enough to evaluate actual risk rather than apply generic best practice
Form independent, well-reasoned opinions on security and architecture decisions, and voice them even when they cut against consensus or a leader's default plan
Push teams to move faster when process or over-engineering is introducing complexity without reducing risk — and push teams to slow down when GTM pressure is outrunning a clear-eyed view of the risk
Debate hard, then align, then commit: help the org land on the right call, then execute on it
Seed and grow a working community of senior ICs embedded in security operations, product security, and enterprise security — connecting people, sharing knowledge, and creating the venues (formal or informal) for that to happen
Lead time-boxed, high-stakes, cross-functional engagements such as M&A security due diligence and partner risk assessments, often with incomplete information and a short runway
Draw on your own expertise where it applies, and quickly figure out how to close knowledge gaps elsewhere — staying accountable for the outcome either way
Requirements
12+ years of experience in security engineering, software engineering, or a related discipline, including senior individual-contributor or technical-lead experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
Deep, credible technical expertise in security, plus working depth across compute, network, and storage architecture
A track record of forming and defending independent technical positions, along with the judgment to know when to stop debating and commit
Experience influencing without formal authority, including with management and cross-functional partners, in both directions — accelerating and slowing down decisions
Comfort owning ambiguous, deadline-driven work such as M&A diligence or partner risk reviews, and being accountable for the result even without the full picture upfront
A genuine interest in mentoring and connecting other senior engineers, without needing a management title to do it

Direct experience leading M&A security due diligence or partner/vendor risk assessments
Background spanning multiple layers of the stack (e.g., network and storage, or application and infrastructure security)

Join Cluster Scalability, one of MongoDB's Online Transaction Processing teams, and help build the core infrastructure that makes MongoDB a world-class distributed database. The team builds the infrastructure and tools that let customers scale their workloads past what a single node can handle. We take pride in building clean abstractions over hard distributed systems problems, so users can focus on their data instead of worrying about where it lives or how it's accessed. Our work has a big impact: it solves the hardest data challenges faced by MongoDB's largest customers.
As a Senior Software Engineer on Cluster Scalability, you'll work on data partitioning, one of the hardest and most impactful problem areas at MongoDB today. You'll collaboratively design and build the distributed machinery that turns independent query-processing and storage nodes into a single, unified database system. Your team’s work will be to build the data-movement and dynamic-scaling features that run on top of it. Current work includes seamless horizontal scaling with minimal tradeoffs, better cluster elasticity and smarter workload execution. You'll solve complex performance problems and design protocols for moving and placing data without disruption. Your work will help the architecture scale reliably to meet customer demand at any volume.
Our team champions a strong culture of inclusivity, diversity, and collaboration. If you want to work on a collaborative team that applies distributed systems fundamentals to deliver core features of a popular database, join us! Let’s change what’s possible for application developers, system architects, and database operators.
This role can be based remotely in British Columbia or Ontario, Canada.
Candidate Profile
5+ years of experience building distributed systems
Experience with building production-level code with a large user base, robust design structure and rigorous code quality, written in C++.
Degree in Computer Science or similar field, or equivalent practical experience, with strong competencies in data structures, algorithms, and software design/architecture
Passion for the theory and practice of system design for large-scale distributed systems, as well as hands-on or academic experience in the domain
Understands modern computer architecture and internals to the degree that they can reason about how specific design choices plays out in a system like MongoDB
Has demonstrated industry success or academic research in areas such as:
High performance / low latency networking
Performance tuning
Distributed systems
System observability
System resiliency
Success Measures
In your first month, you’ll understand the high-level architecture of MongoDB, dive into the details of your team’s components, and resolve a few bugs
In the first three months, you’ll contribute to the development of a project slated for the next release of MongoDB, take on code review responsibilities, and participate in design reviews for new features

The MongoDB Atlas team is a diverse group of contributors working together to help our users manage MongoDB at global scale. We are responsible for MongoDB Atlas: our database as a service offering and fastest growing product which allows users to deploy fault-tolerant, globally distributed MongoDB clusters in just minutes.
We're seeking a Senior Engineer to join the Atlas Identity and Access Management (IAM) team. IAM is a platform and a product team. We serve internal engineers by providing them a secure and durable suite of services, and we serve external customers by providing them user facing features and products. We are the owners of Atlas’ authentication (OAuth, SSO, Federated Identity) and authorization (RBAC, ABAC) systems, along with many others. The IAM team’s mission is to enable customers to securely build their applications with Atlas through our best in class user experience.
The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) is a US government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud products and services. Our FedRAMP program requires that anyone who is accessing customer data or metadata inside the Authorization Boundary be a US Citizen on US Soil.
This role will be based remotely in the United States.

Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Desire to collaborate with colleagues and mentor fellow engineers
Is curious, collaborative, empathetic, and intellectually honest
Has a passion for problem solving and learning new things in the domains of computer science and software engineering

At MongoDB, we are building the future of data platforms with MongoDB Atlas; our fully managed, multi-cloud database service. The Infrastructure Security (InfraSec) team sits within Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) in the CTO organization. We are an engineering team dedicated to building the security infrastructure, primitives, and reusable controls that protect MongoDB Atlas across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud (GCP).

Lead complex technical projects from planning through successful deployment with clear stakeholder updates

Mentor junior engineers and foster a collaborative team environment

5+ years of professional software development experience building, deploying, and operating multi-tenant cloud services with a focus on operational excellence
Experience with large backend/compiled codebases, such as Rust or C/C++
Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms (e.g. Kubernetes)

Experience with distributed systems
Familiarity with database internals or experience building core components for data processing systems
Excellent verbal and written technical communication skills, with a strong desire to collaborate with colleagues
Strong time management skills and the ability to realistically assess project complexity
Demonstrated track record of going above and beyond for customers
Strong candidates may also have
Experience writing and profiling highly performant Rust code
Experience improving reliability through chaos engineering and load testing
Experience building scalable cloud services on multiple cloud provider platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Interest in the theory and practice of high-availability systems (hands-on experience or an M.Sc./Ph.D. in the domain is a plus)

In 3 months, you'll have shipped code into production and collaborated with the team to solve tough problems

Description
MongoDB’s Compliance team leads the strategy, execution, and maintenance of the company’s global security certifications and regulatory requirements. The team translates complex obligations into scalable operational processes and maintains an audit-ready posture across a broad portfolio of frameworks and markets.
The Senior Compliance Analyst is a senior individual-contributor role that leads high-stakes audits and specialized compliance workstreams.
We act as the primary interface between external auditors and our internal Product, Engineering, and Legal teams. Our goal is to translate complex regulatory requirements into scalable operational processes, maintaining a compliant and audit-ready posture across our diverse portfolio.
Senior Technical Compliance Analyst (Public Sector) is a senior-level individual contributor role responsible for the lifecycle management of our most sensitive US government authorizations. This role acts as a lead for high-stakes workstreams involving FedRAMP High, DoD IL5+, CJIS, and ITAR. Unlike the Analyst level, this role takes full ownership of complex federal assessments and leads the continuous monitoring strategy for our Atlas for Government product. This role is a key resource for interpreting NIST 800-53 controls and translating them into technical requirements for our engineering teams. A requirement for this role is to be a US Citizen.
This role will be based remotely in United States.
Key Responsibilities
Lead end-to-end external audits and certifications, coordinating scoping, audit plans, evidence, auditor engagement, findings, and final outcomes
Own internal audit cadences and remediation tracking; establish clear accountability for findings, milestones, dependencies, and resolution timelines, and drive timely follow-through with technical teams
Serve as a lead point of contact for auditors and enterprise customers during security reviews and audit deep-dives; explain MongoDB’s control environment with clarity and confidence
Map regulatory requirements to the central control framework and conduct gap analyses for new frameworks, jurisdictions, and market expansions
Assess compliance-program maturity and report material risks, gaps, trends, and delivery status to team and business leaders
Author and review customer-facing security documentation and audit evidence, ensuring it accurately reflects MongoDB’s controls and architectural guardrails
Lead cross-functional workstreams that advance the ARC roadmap; identify risks and dependencies early and recommend practical improvements to processes and tooling
Build and maintain executive and operational dashboards and Jira workflows for control performance, audit findings, and remediation progress; mentor stakeholders on compliance practices
Lead the end-to-end execution of federal assessments, coordinating with Third Party Assessment Organizations (3PAOs), agency sponsors, and the FedRAMP PMO
Manage the federal continuous monitoring (ConMon) program, including the timely analysis and reporting of vulnerabilities and the maintenance of the POA&M
Lead the annual update and technical review of core FedRAMP artifacts, including the System Security Plan (SSP), Contingency Plan (ISCP), and Incident Response Plan (IRP)
Act as a technical advisor to Engineering and Operations teams to ensure cloud configurations (e.g., FIPS 140-2, boundary protection, and access control) meet federal and DoD IL5+ mandates
Expectations
Operate independently in ambiguous, complex situations and exercise sound judgment with minimal supervision
Take accountability for program outcomes—not only task tracking—and proactively surface risks, trade-offs, and decisions that require escalation
Influence technical and business stakeholders across teams and levels to deliver sustainable compliance outcomes
Communicate regulatory intent and technical control requirements in concise, actionable language for both technical and non-technical audiences
Scope and Complexity
The role manages overlapping audit cycles and compliance work across international jurisdictions and across highly regulated sectors such as financial services, healthcare, and government. Work ranges from complex evidence and control assessments to interpreting emerging requirements and identifying how controls can satisfy multiple standards.
The scope is deeply technical and specialized for the US Federal, State, and Local Government markets.
You will navigate the complexity of mapping shared controls across multiple specialized frameworks, ensuring a single remediation effort satisfies FedRAMP, CJIS, and ITAR requirements simultaneously.
Authority and Impact
The Senior Compliance Analyst has the authority to lead federal assessment project streams and represent MongoDB in technical reviews with 3PAOs and federal agencies.Your work directly enables MongoDB to secure and maintain the authorizations required to serve the Department of Defense and civilian agencies, protecting a critical revenue stream.
Expertise and Leadership
The role develops deep subject-matter expertise in assigned frameworks and in how MongoDB’s cloud architecture satisfies their requirements. It serves as a trusted resource for mapping technical evidence to regulatory intent, leads complex projects such as internal audits and framework renewals, and mentors colleagues and partner teams on effective compliance practices.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (such as Information Systems, Computer Science, or Cybersecurity), or equivalent practical experience
7+ years of experience in GRC, Information Security, or IT Audit, preferably in a SaaS or cloud environment, with a heavy focus on US Public Sector frameworks (FedRAMP, DoD SRG, CJIS)
Demonstrated experience leading technical audits or compliance programs
Strong understanding of cloud security principles, risk management, and how controls operate in a cloud-native environment across AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure
Deep understanding of NIST 800-53 and NIST 800-171 controls and how they are implemented within cloud architectures (AWS, GCP, or Azure)
Proven track record of managing federal audits from kickoff through to the issuance of an Authorization to Operate (ATO)
Exceptional ability to explain complex security configurations to government auditors and internal technical teams
Advanced proficiency in Jira and Confluence to track control performance data and manage large-scale federal documentation projects
Practical experience performing control mapping, gap analyses, remediation oversight, and program or control-maturity assessments
Advanced proficiency with Jira or similar tools for managing audit findings, control data, and high-volume remediation workflows
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to lead auditor/customer discussions and translate technical requirements for non-technical audiences

MongoDB’s Storage Layer Services (SLS) team is re-architecting the MongoDB cloud storage layer and sits at the heart of our next-generation cloud storage architecture. This relatively new team is building performant, multi-tenant distributed storage services that both enhance today’s Atlas storage stack and enable more customer workloads to run more efficiently.
You will partner with the teams building these storage services to define SLOs, shape capacity plans, and ensure the reliability, durability, and operational safety of the storage layer that underpins Atlas. You’ll join a small, senior team of SREs as founding members of this organization, playing a crucial role in executing on a multi-year roadmap for MongoDB’s cloud storage architecture.
This role can be based out of our Boston, New York City, Raleigh, Miami, Pittsburgh or remotely in the United States while physically based in an Eastern or Central time zone location.
The ideal candidate should
Have 6+ years of experience working on software development and operating distributed systems
Proficiency in Python, Go, or a similar language
Have operated or supported stateful storage or database systems at scale, and are comfortable with durability, consistency, and recovery trade-offs.
Possess a customer-focused mindset
Value efficiency in processes and operations
Prefer automation over manual processes. We are a small team of software engineers with a strong bias towards software solutions to avoid toil
Experience using and extending containerization technologies, particularly Kubernetes, to enhance application agility, optimize resource utilization, and accelerate time-to-market
Expertise in cloud infrastructure platforms, including AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Azure
Understanding of Linux operating system internals and networking concepts (e.g., TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, routing)
Responsibilities
Work on our multi-tenant distributed storage systems, balancing long-term strategic infrastructure goals with immediate engineering needs
Build for reliability, making services and infrastructure available, resilient, fault-tolerant, and self-healing
Identify and configure key metrics to detect incidents and quantify service health, availability, and performance
Participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation to resolve issues involving the storage infrastructure
Become an expert in infrastructure performance, helping us optimize from the application level all the way to the kernel
Strong candidates may also have experience with:
Leading major architectural shifts, such as moving from legacy storage stacks to new multi-tenant storage architectures, including planning and executing large-scale data and workload migrations with tight availability and durability requirements
Managing and scaling infrastructure across multi-cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure)
Designing secure, multi-tenant runtime environments at scale

As General Manager, you’ll have significant autonomy to shape a more self-sufficient business by integrating Clarity’s federal engineering and modernization capabilities with MongoDB’s product and go-to-market teams, expanding our position in Defense, and establishing the partnerships, authorization strategy, talent, and operating discipline needed for sustained growth.

You will shape how Clarity’s people and capabilities work alongside MongoDB by aligning strategy, customer engagement, delivery, and operating practices while preserving the specialized expertise federal customers rely on.
MongoDB Atlas for Government’s pursuit of FedRAMP Certified – Class D (formerly known as FedRAMP High) expands MongoDB’s ability to support high-impact government workloads, secure AI, and mission-critical modernization across cloud environments. This is an opportunity to build on customer trust and strong executive commitment, address significant unmet demand across government, and shape a business with the ambition and resources to become a meaningful growth engine for MongoDB.
We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Washington DC for our hybrid working model.
What you will do
Own the public-sector P&L, strategy, operating plan, and execution, with accountability for revenue, expenses, investment decisions, forecast quality, and overall performance; Establish executive-grade forecasting, pipeline inspection, P&L reviews, account and partner planning, talent reviews, and cross-functional decision mechanisms that strengthen predictability and scalable execution
Lead and develop the Regional Directors and their sales teams, together with dedicated Finance, Sales Operations, Product, Solutions Architecture, and Customer Success resources; Set shared goals, clarify decision rights, and establish effective interfaces with MongoDB’s broader functional organizations
Build an increasingly autonomous, high-performing public-sector entity by setting its governance, resource priorities, operating cadence, and talent systems, while applying MongoDB’s company-wide processes and the practices needed to serve government customers; Make timely decisions with substantial autonomy, create clarity as the organization evolves, and balance near-term results with long-term scale
Integrate Clarity’s people and federal services capabilities into the public-sector business; Align strategy, leadership, accountability, customer engagement, delivery, and partner motions; clarify how Clarity works with MongoDB’s sales, Product, Solutions Architecture, Customer Success, and Security teams; and shape the organization’s reporting model and long-term end state
Grow strategic Federal civilian relationships and expand MongoDB’s position in Defense by building trust with Department of Defense and other mission stakeholders, converting existing product usage into strategic customer relationships, and developing repeatable paths to new opportunities
Build and scale a partner ecosystem, with a strong emphasis on systems integrators alongside resellers and other strategic partners; Create joint customer and delivery motions that extend MongoDB’s reach and support mission-relevant outcomes
